title: Effective, Chemical-Free Pest Control for Outdoor Plants
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 11, 2026
review: These yellow sticky traps have been incredibly effective for my outdoor plants. I placed them around my garden beds and containers, and they immediately started catching flying pests like whiteflies, fungus gnats, and small aphids. Within a week I noticed fewer bugs around my plants and healthier new growth.They’re easy to set up, hold up well outdoors, and stay sticky even with sun and watering nearby. I also appreciate that they help control pests without using chemical sprays around my garden. Simple, affordable, and surprisingly effective — I’ll definitely keep using them throughout the growing season.

title: Sticky to the Icky Bugs!
date: Reviewed in the United States on July 22, 2025
review: Oh, these things work so well it isn't even funny...kind of scary, actually...very sticky, great value, and easy as pie to use.  You will definitely get the first one stuck to YOU, but you'll figure out how to hold them and use them properly. (they are HELLA sticky--be warned!).The gnats have been just dreadful this year, and I think I may have bought a bag of Miracle Grow indoor soil that was infested with them. I suspect so, anyway. Most annoying little so-and-sos.Included in this package was the 60 double-sided sticky pest eliminators, along with some "extra" little cute and fun indoor plant stakes, a tiny shovel, and some twisty wire. Don't know what I'll ever use that tiny shovel for, but it's really cute! Great product...would be nice if I didn't have to rebuy them, but...lol!

title: Great Gnat Traps!
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 2, 2026
review: These fly traps are definitely doing their job. The gnats seem to love them, and they stay pretty well stuck in the soil.I’m still trying to get rid of gnats in my plants and it’s been a lot of work, but these traps at least help me see what’s going on and whether what I’m doing is actually working or not.They do work, which is kind of a double-edged sword because you don’t want the gnats, but seeing them on the traps means they’re actually catching them.**I will say, keep them away from kids and pets since they are very sticky. And apparently also teens… I didn’t think I needed to warn my 14-year-old daughter, but I definitely do now. She somehow got one stuck in her hair, which still makes no sense to me, but here we are.Overall, I’m hoping to start seeing cleaner traps soon with fewer gnats, but they are clearly doing their job.
